purpose: Lasmiditan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults, with or without aura. It helps relieve the pain and other symptoms of a migraine attack once it has already started. It is not used every day to prevent migraines — only taken when a migraine begins.
how_it_works: Lasmiditan works by targeting a specific receptor in the brain called the 5-HT1F receptor, which helps calm down the pain signals involved in a migraine. Unlike older migraine medicines called triptans, it does not tighten blood vessels, which makes it an option for people who cannot take triptans. Think of it as a 'signal blocker' that tells your brain to turn down the migraine pain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, feeling sleepy or tired, tingling or numbness (especially in the hands, feet, or face), feeling strange or 'not yourself,' and nausea. These effects are usually temporary but can be strong right after taking the medication.
warnings: This medication can seriously impair your ability to drive or operate machinery — you must NOT drive or use heavy equipment for at least 8 hours after taking it, even if you feel okay. It can cause central nervous system (CNS) depression, meaning it can slow down your brain and reactions. It is a controlled substance (Schedule V) because it has some potential for misuse. Tell your doctor if you take other medications that affect serotonin, as there is a risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine. It has not been studied enough in pregnancy, so talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 50 mg, 100 mg, or 200 mg taken by mouth as a single tablet when your migraine starts. If the first dose does not fully work, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours later, but do not take more than one dose in a 24-hour period. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Take it with or without food.
